exampleAnswers.Purpose and audience: An offsite agenda with outcomes, preparation, facilitation, and space for recovery.
exampleAnswers.Working context: This fictional one-day offsite gives a small team time to review its working habits and choose two improvements. The venue, catering, and access arrangements remain items for the organizer to confirm.
exampleAnswers.Example records:
Time: 09:30 · Session: Arrive and settle · Output: Shared purpose
Time: 10:00 · Session: What is slowing us down? · Output: Three concrete observations
Time: 11:30 · Session: Work on one problem · Output: Options and tradeoffs
Time: 14:00 · Session: Choose two experiments · Output: Owners and review date
Time: 15:30 · Session: Close and travel buffer · Output: Written recap
exampleAnswers.Content decisions:
Prepare lightly: Ask each person for one example of work that flowed well and one that became difficult. Share the agenda early and allow written contributions for people who think better before a discussion.
Facilitate the decision: Describe the problem before proposing solutions. Give quieter participants time to contribute, record disagreement accurately, and make the decision rule clear.
Follow through: The offsite is complete when the experiments have owners, a small first step, and a review date. Keep the recap short enough that the team can return to it during ordinary work.
exampleAnswers.Format and interaction: schedule layout; section navigation and expandable detail where useful; matching portrait document PDF.
exampleAnswers.Sharing and provenance: A hypothetical example informed by Claw Me’s small-team and Agent workflows. These are not Pete’s actual clients, finances, travel plans, research results, or commitments. Keep the real adaptation private until the owner chooses to share.
